page: Amazon Web Services i8g.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The host utilizes AWS Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.8 GHz, supplying 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs without hyperthreading. Memory resources scale to 768.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is configured with 22,500 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 56 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute and data throughput performance. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 163,578.54 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 26,076.0, both within the top 10% bracket. Single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,706.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,894.0. Memory throughput reaches 480.68 GB/sec on large-block read tests and 217.89 GB/sec on large-block write tests, supporting heavy data shuffling. Database and caching metrics reflect this capability, with PassMark database operations reaching 47,378.63 and Redis SET operations processing 194.36 million operations per second.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the balance between average single-threaded execution speeds and extensive parallel processing potential. While workloads heavily reliant on single-core clock velocity may see average results, the density of 96 dedicated cores and 768.0 GB of memory makes the server cost-efficient for scaled, concurrent I/O pipelines. Workloads well matched to this profile include large-scale distributed databases, in-memory caches, high-throughput static web serving, real-time analytics engines, and high-concurrency Clang software compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.24xlarge is a storage-optimized server utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor and 64-bit ARM AWS Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 96 dedicated physical cores (96 vCPUs) clocked at 2.8 GHz, 768.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core), and 22,500 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, supported by 56 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. GPU acceleration is absent. Benchmark results show average single-threaded speed offset by top-tier multi-core compute, high memory bandwidth (480.68 GB/sec read), and high I/O throughput, highlighted by 194.36 million Redis SET operations per second and 47,378.63 PassMark database operations. With substantial local NVMe storage and dedicated core density, the instance offers strong cost efficiency for high-density, concurrent storage operations, making it suitable for distributed transactional databases, real-time analytics, caching platforms, and parallel compilation tasks.
